(def pr-sequential-writer
  (fn [writer print-one begin sep end opts coll]
  (let [dup (pr-opts-dup opts)]
  (binding [*print-level* (and (not dup) *print-level* (dec *print-level*))]
    (if (and *print-level* (neg? *print-level*))
      (-write writer "#")
      (do
        (-write writer begin)
        (let [xs (seq coll)]
          (when xs
            (loop [x (first xs) xs (next xs) n (and (not dup) (pr-opts-len opts))]
              (if (and n (zero? n))
                (-write writer (or (:more-marker opts) "..."))
                (do
                  (print-one x writer opts)
                  (when xs
                    (-write writer sep)
                    (recur (first xs) (next xs) (and n (dec n)))))))))
        (-write writer end)))))))
rationale: Expand defn to def/fn and follow Clojure's print-sequential (#302), keeping the signature, opts and :more-marker. *print-level* and *print-length* are off when logical false or under *print-dup*, as in Clojure. Each step takes the next element before printing, as Clojure's [x & xs] destructuring does, so an unchunked lazy seq is realized exactly as far as Clojure realizes it, and a hidden level realizes none of it.
